verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same algorithmic fix to `mergeContacts`, so correctness, scope and design are effectively equal. A's added test pins a behavior the Map rewrite could easily have broken: when the stored book already has duplicate emails, the first one still wins. B instead adds a wall-clock timing assertion, which depends on the machine and does not guard semantics. A's report is also cleaner and openly states what it did not verify, while B's ends with an irrelevant line about unavailable tools.
a_issues: No automated guard against a performance regression; the speedup is only shown by an out-of-repo benchmark.
The benchmark compared only output counts, not the merged contents (the report says so).
b_issues: The regression test relies on a machine-dependent 1 s threshold, which may flake on slow CI runners.
Adds no test for the first-duplicate-wins edge case that the Map rewrite must preserve.
The report ends with an irrelevant, confusing remark about 'Crapper and Mutator tools'.
No comment explaining the purpose of the index map.

verdict.rationale: The production change is the same in both: a Map from normalized email to its first index, with new arrivals registered so duplicates inside one upload still merge. B's version adds a helpful comment. B's new test pins a subtle behavior the rewrite could easily break: the first existing duplicate still wins, which is what the `!has` guard protects. A's new test is a wall-clock timing assertion that depends on the machine and does not protect any behavioral edge case.
a_issues: The added test asserts elapsed time under 1 s, which can be flaky on slow CI machines.
No test covers first-entry-wins when the stored book already has duplicate emails, so the `!indexByEmail.has(key)` guard is unprotected.
The report ends with a stray, irrelevant remark about 'Crapper and Mutator tools'.
b_issues: No test guards against a performance regression; the speedup is backed only by an out-of-repo benchmark.
The report admits the benchmark output was not compared field by field with the old implementation.
